newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude called slightly up tracking ACCESS.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude called slightly up tracking ACCESS.

text.p: NYMEX crude was called slightly higher Thursday tracking ACCESS on little news as oil prices were seen searching for direction in rangebound trade.
"There is not much in the way of news. We are rangebound, and we could easily ease off a bit after rising at the open," said a New York crude trader.
Crude was called five to 10 cents a barrel higher while refined products were called steady to up 0.25 cent a gallon.
Pompt gasoline was seen technically weakened after its session high Wednesday of 63.10 cents failed before hitting resistance of 63.20 cents, set by Tuesday's spot session high.
Strong distillate demand in Asia was supporting gas oil prices in London which was expected to help heating oil here, dealers said.
In Singapore, a new one-day diesel trading record was made Thursday with the sale of 2.44 million barrels in 16 physical cargoes to three traders.
On London's IPE, May gas oil was up $1.50 at $164.50 a tonne. June Brent was up 10 cents a barrel at $18.16.
In Middle East news, Kuwait officially informed the United Nations late Wednesday about an Iraqi boat opening fire at two Kuwaiti vessels on April 12.
Since the market factored in the incident two weeks ago, dealers expected the latest development to have little impact.
On Wedensday, June crude ended 14 cents a barrel higher at $19.73. May heating oil settled 0.82 cent higher at 55.65 cents a gallon while May gasoline settled 0.03 cent a gallon lower at 61.74 cents.

June crude's 14-day Relative Strength Indicator was a neutral 46.27 with technical support seen between the simple 20-day and 18-day moving averages of $19.71 and $19.62 respectively on the spot continuation chart.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
